financials_interim.notes: Associated Motor Finance Company PLC (AMF) is a licensed finance company (NBFI) -- single entity, no Group/Company split, no segment reporting disclosed (note 3: 'the company does not have any operating segment... for which discrete financial information is available'). IMPORTANT CONTEXT: this is very likely AMF's LAST published quarterly interim financial statement as an independent listed entity -- note 5 discloses that L B Finance PLC (LBF) has completed a Mandatory Offer and holds 82,848,928 shares (73.11%), shareholders approved amalgamation of AMF into LBF at an EGM on 30 June 2026 (i.e. the last day of this reporting quarter), the amalgamation's effective date is 31 July 2026, AMF share trading was suspended from 27 July 2026, and non-LBF shareholders will receive a cash consideration of Rs.55.00/share (not a share exchange). This is flagged as critical context for interpretation, not merely a subsequent event footnote. shares_in_issue: not stated as a single explicit figure in this filing; derived and cross-checked three ways, all converging exactly on 113,341,342 -- (i) LBF's stated stake of 82,848,928 shares = 73.11% of 113,341,342; (ii) Public Holding of 30,467,372 shares = 26.88% of 113,341,342; (iii) Twenty Largest Holders total of 97,570,322 shares = 86.09% of 113,341,342. This also ties EPS (249,835,055 /113,341,342 = 2.204, rounds to disclosed 2.20) and NAVPS (4,898,559,934/113,341,342 = 43.22, ties disclosed 43.22 exactly). revenue = 'Total operating income' (1,210,827,371), the filing's own subtotal = Net Interest Income (1,122,745,294) + Fee & commission income (27,645,671) + Net trading income (2,823,960) + Other operating income net (57,612,446). operating_profit = 'Profit before taxes on financial services' (514,595,719), the company's own pre-VATFS subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK -- Interest Income (1,590,748,637) and Interest Expenses (468,003,343) are disclosed as separate gross lines but netted to an explicit 'Net Interest Income' subtotal before Total operating income (same structure as AFSL/ALLI/CDB/AAF this session), so populating them separately would double count against revenue. tax_expense = 'Income tax (expense)/reversals' (151,651,829) only; 'Tax on financial services' (113,108,835) is a separate VAT-on-Financial-Services-type levy sitting between operating_profit and profit_before_tax, consistent with this session's other NBFI entries. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split; 'Financial assets at amortized cost / loans and lease receivables' is the core lending book, not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks and financial institutions' (1,155,444,384) -- no debentures or other longer-dated instrument is disclosed, and this is the only interest-bearing debt line besides deposits, so it is classified short-term per the AFSL/CDB convention for bank borrowings absent a maturity split; long_term_borrowings left blank. 'Deposits from customers' (14,236,683,725) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt, per project convention. cash_and_equivalents = 'Cash and cash equivalents' (221,844,516), consistent between the Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Statement (no bank overdraft component here, unlike some peers). capex = 'Purchase of property and equipment, intangible assets & ROU Asset' (6,515,935) -- disclosed as a single combined cash-flow line, cannot be disaggregated into PP&E/intangibles/ROU components from this filing; used as-is (this is a genuine gap, noted below). Impairment/NPL commentary: 'Impairment charges on financial assets & other losses' more than doubled, from Rs.163,545,589 (Q1 FY25/26) to Rs.396,128,245 (Q1 FY26/27), +142% -- by far the single largest driver of the 17% YoY decline in Profit for the Period, more than offsetting an 8% rise in Net Interest Income and a 33% rise in Fee and commission income. Efficiency Ratio (impairment-adjusted) worsened to 36.84% (30-Jun-26) from 34.48% (30-Jun-25) per the disclosed KPI table, consistent with this impairment deterioration. Personnel Expenses fell 19% (Rs.228.5mn to Rs.185.1mn), a partial offset.

interim_updates.note_text: CONTEXT THAT OVERRIDES EVERYTHING ELSE: this is very likely the last quarterly result AMF publishes as a stand-alone listed company. L B Finance PLC (LFIN) holds 73.11% (82,848,928 shares) after a Mandatory Offer; shareholders approved amalgamation into LBF at the EGM on 30 June 2026; the effective date is 31 July 2026; AMF trading was suspended from the close of 27 July 2026; and minority holders receive Rs.55.00 per share in CASH (no share swap). Rs.55.00 compares with a last traded price of Rs.52.70 at 30 June, a quarter high of Rs.64.80, and a NAV/share of Rs.43.22 (a 1.27x price-to-book exit). On the numbers: Total Operating Income rose 8% to Rs.1,210.8mn in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), but Profit Before Tax fell 17% to Rs.401.5mn and PAT 17% to Rs.249.8mn (EPS Rs.2.20 vs Rs.2.65), because Impairment Charges more than doubled (+142%) to Rs.396.1mn from Rs.163.5mn -- a Rs.232.6mn hit. Before impairment the business actually improved: income less operating expenses rose about 16% (Rs.910.7mn vs Rs.788.0mn) as Personnel Expenses fell 19% to Rs.185.1mn (Rs.228.5mn) and depreciation fell 18%, even though Other Operating Expenses rose 23% to Rs.99.0mn. Core income was only modestly higher: Net Interest Income +2% to Rs.1,122.7mn (Interest Income +4% to Rs.1,590.7mn vs Interest Expense +9% to Rs.468.0mn), and Fee & Commission Income +33% to Rs.27.6mn; the rest of the 8% revenue growth came from 'Other operating income (net)' of Rs.57.6mn versus just Rs.0.5mn a year ago (a Rs.57.1mn non-recurring-looking swing -- excluding it, total income grew ~3%). The balance sheet shrank: total assets -4% in the quarter to Rs.21.4bn, with customer deposits down 8.7% (Rs.1.36bn outflow) to Rs.14.24bn -- likely reflecting the takeover uncertainty -- and loans/lease receivables down 3.5% to Rs.18.16bn; AMF drew Rs.700mn of bank borrowings (repaid Rs.150mn) to fund the outflow, taking Due to Banks to Rs.1.16bn from Rs.0.60bn, and operating cash flow was -Rs.571.1mn (vs -Rs.3.1mn). The liquid-asset buffer fell sharply to 125.5% of requirement (330.0% a year earlier; minimum 100%). Annualised ROE fell to 20.93% from 29.18%; Total capital adequacy 18.83% (min 12.5%); LRA rating BB (Stable).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no predecessor quarter is stored for AMF (first financial_statements entry). The filing discloses no segment information (single reporting line). AMF is expected to cease to exist as a listed entity on 31 July 2026 (amalgamation effective date) -- any later 'current' data for this symbol should not be expected, and market_data for AMF may be stale after the 27 July 2026 trading suspension.
interim_updates.takeaway: For minority holders the investment case is now the Rs.55.00 cash exit (1.27x NAV, ~4% above the last traded price), not the earnings. Operationally the quarter shows a pre-provision improvement (cost cuts, +16%) overwhelmed by a 142% jump in impairment charges, while deposits and loans both shrank -- AMF was being run down ahead of its absorption into LB Finance.

operational_highlights: Amalgamation into L B Finance (LFIN): LBF holds 73.11%; EGM approval 30 June 2026; effective 31 July 2026; AMF trading suspended from 27 July 2026; minorities get Rs.55.00/share in cash vs last traded Rs.52.70 and NAV Rs.43.22 (1.27x)
PBT -17% to Rs.401.5mn, PAT -17% to Rs.249.8mn (EPS Rs.2.20 vs Rs.2.65) despite Total Operating Income +8% to Rs.1,210.8mn
Impairment Charges +142% to Rs.396.1mn (from Rs.163.5mn) -- a Rs.232.6mn hit that drove the entire profit decline
Pre-provision profit up ~16% (Rs.910.7mn vs Rs.788.0mn) as Personnel Expenses fell 19% to Rs.185.1mn; Net Interest Income only +2% (Rs.1,122.7mn)
'Other operating income' Rs.57.6mn vs Rs.0.5mn a year ago inflated revenue growth; excluding it total income grew ~3%
Customer deposits -8.7% in the quarter to Rs.14.24bn (Rs.1.36bn outflow); loans/leases -3.5% to Rs.18.16bn; bank borrowings up to Rs.1.16bn; operating cash flow -Rs.571.1mn
Liquid assets 125.5% of requirement (vs 330.0% a year earlier); Total CAR 18.83%; annualised ROE 20.93% (29.18%); NAV/share Rs.43.22 (Rs.41.02 at March 2026)
key_drivers: Impairment charge +142% (Rs.163.5mn to Rs.396.1mn): the sole reason PBT fell 17% -- pre-provision profit actually rose ~16%
Personnel Expenses -19% (Rs.228.5mn to Rs.185.1mn) and depreciation -18% lifted pre-provision profit despite Other Operating Expenses +23%
Other operating income of Rs.57.6mn (vs Rs.0.5mn) flattered the 8% revenue growth; underlying income growth ~3% with NII +2%
Takeover-related run-off: deposits -Rs.1.36bn and loans/leases shrinking, funded by Rs.700mn of new bank borrowings, shrinking the liquidity buffer to 125.5% of requirement
